ai.name: Apple vs OpenAI
ai.hook: Apple sues OpenAI and Jony Ive's io, alleging **400+ employees** funneled hardware secrets.
insights: Filed in a California court, Apple accuses OpenAI/io of systematically extracting confidential device info via recruited ex-employees
Ben Thompson frames it as Apple 'lashing out' at a structural problem, not a clean IP theft case
Signals just how much a real AI hardware race for the next device category is heating up
ai.for_you: No direct action, but worth watching as a signal that the next hardware wave (not just software agents) is where the real fight is moving.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Biggest AI-adjacent legal story of the week, cross-covered by Stratechery and PT press

ai.name: Claude Code vs OpenCode token overhead
ai.hook: Claude Code burns **33k tokens** before it even reads your prompt, OpenCode needs only **7k**.
insights: 597 points, 323 comments, one of the hottest HN threads of the week
Overhead comes from system prompt bloat and tool definitions loaded on every call
Directly affects real cost-per-task for anyone running agents at volume
ai.for_you: If you're billing PT SMB clients per-task or per-agent-run, this is the kind of overhead that quietly eats your margin, worth checking which harness/tool you're actually using under the hood.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Top-voted HN post today, directly relevant to agent cost economics

video.title: Switching from Claude Code to Codex CLI #claudecode #ai #codex #google #anthropic #tech #reddit

ai.name: GPT-5.6 production migration
ai.hook: One team's real migration to GPT-5.6 hits **2.2x faster** and **27% cheaper** in production.
insights: Documented case study, not a benchmark claim, on an actual live agent
Cost and latency gains both material, not marginal
Adds real evidence behind OpenAI's 'best model we've made' claim from launch week
ai.for_you: Worth a real cost/speed test on whatever agent workflow you're running for the agency, this is the kind of concrete before/after case you can replicate on your own client work this week.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Rare real-world migration data point vs. the usual benchmark noise

ai.name: 'Stop Telling Me to Ask an LLM'
ai.hook: A widely-shared essay pushes back hard on AI-as-default-answer culture.
insights: 206 points, 121 comments, strong engagement for an opinion piece
Argues reflexive 'just ask AI' advice erodes actual expertise and trust
Resonates with growing fatigue narrative around AI-first UX
ai.for_you: Good gut-check for how you position the agency to PT SMB owners, some clients will resent being told 'just use ChatGPT', your value is doing the judgment work they don't want to do themselves.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Strong HN discussion, useful counter-narrative to filter out of pitch decks

ai.name: Craig Mod
ai.hook: Cut his newsletter tooling bill from **$7,000/year to $150** by rebuilding it himself with AI.
insights: Replaced Campaign Monitor entirely with a custom AI-built tool
Calls it the start of a 'golden age of tool building' where anyone builds bespoke software instead of buying incumbent SaaS
Still draws a hard line: uses AI as research assistant, refuses to let it write his actual prose
ai.for_you: This is the exact pitch for your micro-SaaS bet: PT SMBs paying for bloated generic tools could get a cheap, custom, AI-built replacement instead, Mod's Campaign Monitor swap is a template case study to literally reference in a pitch.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Most concrete builder story of the week with a real before/after number

ai.name: Grok 4.5
ai.hook: xAI ships a **1.5 trillion parameter** coding model priced for volume, not benchmark bragging rights.
insights: $2/1M input, $6/1M output tokens, 3x larger than Grok 4.3
Musk calls it 'Opus-class' but faster and cheaper
Cursor co-trained it and calls it their most powerful model yet
ai.for_you: Worth a quick side-by-side cost test against GPT-5.6 Sol for any agentic coding tasks you run for clients, capability-per-dollar is exactly the metric that matters for agency margins.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Major frontier release this week, still relevant given Cursor partnership angle

build_this.name: GPT-5.6 production migration case study
build_this.what_it_is: A documented real-world migration of a live AI agent from an older model to GPT-5.6, showing 2.2x speed and 27% cost improvement.
build_this.why_try_it: Run this exact before/after comparison on one of your agency's client workflows this week, you'll have a concrete number to show a PT SMB owner instead of a vague 'AI is better now' pitch.

build_this.name: prompts.chat (Awesome ChatGPT Prompts)
build_this.what_it_is: A large, open, self-hostable library of shared prompts you can run privately for a team or client.
build_this.why_try_it: Self-host a private, branded version of this for your agency clients as a lightweight deliverable, an easy low-effort product to bundle into your first paid engagements without building anything from scratch.

build_this.name: paperless-ngx
build_this.what_it_is: Open-source document management system that scans, indexes, and archives documents automatically.
build_this.why_try_it: PT SMBs (clinics, contabilistas, small law firms) drown in paper and PDFs, this plus an AI layer for extraction/classification is a very sellable 'digitize your office' package for the agency.

podcasts.episode: How a Writer Uses AI Without Losing His Voice
podcasts.takeaway: Craig Mod proves solo builders can now replace expensive SaaS with custom AI-built tools at a fraction of the cost.
key_points: Cut newsletter tooling cost from $7,000/year to $150 by rebuilding it with AI
Calls this the start of a 'golden age of tool building' for non-developers
Still refuses to let AI write his actual prose, uses it strictly as a research assistant
podcasts.for_you: Literally the case study to use when pitching PT SMBs on replacing their expensive generic SaaS subscriptions with a cheap custom tool your agency builds for them.

video.title: How a Writer Uses AI Without Losing His Voice

podcasts.takeaway: Booking.com's CEO argues no company, including his own, has a durable competitive moat anymore in the AI era.
key_points: Glenn Fogel says today's advantage 'is gonna go away tomorrow'
Framed around how AI erodes traditional distribution and search moats
Relevant to any founder betting on defensibility through product alone
podcasts.for_you: Reinforces why the agency's real moat has to be relationships and delivery speed with PT SMBs, not any specific AI tool or workflow you use today, since that will be commoditized fast.

tech.name: OpenAI household push
tech.hook: ChatGPT goes deeper into family use cases, betting on households as the next growth surface.
tech.key_point: Continues the family-oriented positioning already flagged Sunday, now with dedicated feature rollout coverage.
tech.for_you: No direct action for the agency, this targets consumer households not SMBs, filed for awareness.

tech.name: Waze AI voice features

tech.key_point: Google integrates Gemini directly into a mass-market consumer app, not just a chatbot layer.

tech.name: EU social media age limits

tech.for_you: A good reminder that small, sharply-scoped utility tools with zero AI still find an audience, a useful sanity check when scoping your micro-SaaS idea.
